20:1.sourceText: Τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ ἔρχεται πρωῒ σκοτίας ἔτι οὔσης εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ βλέπει τὸν λίθον ἠρμένον ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου.
20:1.targetText: And on the first [day] of the weeks, Mary the Magdalene comes early (there being yet darkness) to the tomb, and she sees the stone having been taken away out of the tomb;

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English day explains the feminine ordinal first in the weekly expression; no day noun is printed in Greek.

20:2.sourceText: τρέχει οὖν καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς Σίμωνα Πέτρον καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἄλλον μαθητὴν ὃν ἐφίλει ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἦραν τὸν Κύριον ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου, καὶ οὐκ οἴδαμεν ποῦ ἔθηκαν αὐτόν.
20:2.targetText: she runs, therefore, and comes to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple whom Jesus was cherishing, and says to them, “They took away the Lord out of the tomb, and we have not known where they laid Him.”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

20:3.sourceText: Ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ Πέτρος καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητής, καὶ ἤρχοντο εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον.
20:3.targetText: Peter, therefore, went forth, and the other disciple, and they were coming to the tomb,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

20:4.sourceText: ἔτρεχον δὲ οἱ δύο ὁμοῦ· καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητὴς προέδραμεν τάχιον τοῦ Πέτρου καὶ ἦλθεν πρῶτος εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον,
20:4.targetText: and the two were running together, and the other disciple ran forward more quickly than Peter, and came first to the tomb,

20:5.sourceText: καὶ παρακύψας βλέπει κείμενα τὰ ὀθόνια, οὐ μέντοι εἰσῆλθεν.
20:5.targetText: and having stooped down, sees the linen clothes lying, yet, indeed, he did not enter.

groups.note: The one adversative/emphatic particle μέντοι is expanded as yet, indeed in LSV; both English particles share that actual source word.

20:6.sourceText: ἔρχεται οὖν καὶ Σίμων Πέτρος ἀκολουθῶν αὐτῷ, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον· καὶ θεωρεῖ τὰ ὀθόνια κείμενα,
20:6.targetText: Simon Peter, therefore, comes, following him, and he entered into the tomb, and beholds the linen clothes lying [there],

unmappedSource.reason: Greek καί also accompanies Simon Peters coming; LSV has no separate also counterpart at this point.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English locative there is supplied with lying; no locative word occurs in Greek here.

20:7.sourceText: καὶ τὸ σουδάριον, ὃ ἦν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ, οὐ μετὰ τῶν ὀθονίων κείμενον ἀλλὰ χωρὶς ἐντετυλιγμένον εἰς ἕνα τόπον.
20:7.targetText: and the napkin that was on His head not lying with the linen clothes, but apart, having been folded up, in one place;

groups.note: Greek εἰς gives the fold-in-one-place arrangement, rendered in by LSV.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

20:8.sourceText: τότε οὖν εἰσῆλθεν καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητὴς ὁ ἐλθὼν πρῶτος εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ εἶδεν καὶ ἐπίστευσεν·
20:8.targetText: then, therefore, the other disciple who came first to the tomb entered also, and he saw and believed;

20:9.sourceText: οὐδέπω γὰρ ᾔδεισαν τὴν γραφὴν, ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι.
20:9.targetText: for they did not yet know the Writing, that it was necessary for Him to rise again out of the dead.

groups.note: Greek present it is necessary is rendered past it was necessary in LSV.

20:10.sourceText: ἀπῆλθον οὖν πάλιν πρὸς αὑτοὺς οἱ μαθηταί.
20:10.targetText: The disciples therefore went away again to their own friends,

groups.note: The Greek reflexive themselves in the returning-to-their-own expression is rendered their own; the additional friends noun is separately noted rather than treated as a Greek friend word.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV supplies friends as the destination people; N1904 has only the reflexive themselves/ones own, without a friend noun.

20:11.sourceText: Μαρία δὲ εἱστήκει πρὸς τῷ μνημείῳ ἔξω κλαίουσα. ὡς οὖν ἔκλαιεν, παρέκυψεν εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον,
20:11.targetText: and Mary was standing near the tomb, weeping outside; as she was weeping, then, she stooped down into the tomb, and beholds two messengers in white, sitting,

review.note: The closing messenger description belongs to raw Greek 20:12. Actual source references preserve its boundary while the English phrase appears in 20:11.

20:12.sourceText: καὶ θεωρεῖ δύο ἀγγέλους ἐν λευκοῖς καθεζομένους, ἕνα πρὸς τῇ κεφαλῇ καὶ ἕνα πρὸς τοῖς ποσίν, ὅπου ἔκειτο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
20:12.targetText: one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had been laid.

sourceMoved.reason: Raw Greek 20:12 begins and beholds two messengers in white sitting; LSV renders those actual words at the end of 20:11, with explicit foreign-reference anchors there.

20:13.sourceText: καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῇ ἐκεῖνοι Γύναι, τί κλαίεις; λέγει αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ἦραν τὸν Κύριόν μου, καὶ οὐκ οἶδα ποῦ ἔθηκαν αὐτόν.
20:13.targetText: And they say to her, “Woman, why do you weep?” She says to them, “Because they took away my Lord, and I have not known where they laid Him”;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

20:14.sourceText: ταῦτα εἰποῦσα ἐστράφη εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω, καὶ θεωρεῖ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἑστῶτα, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν.
20:14.targetText: and having said these things, she turned backward, and sees Jesus standing, and she had not known that it is Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds an opening and; N1904 begins these things having said without an opening conjunction.

20:15.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς Γύναι, τί κλαίεις; τίνα ζητεῖς; ἐκείνη δοκοῦσα ὅτι ὁ κηπουρός ἐστιν, λέγει αὐτῷ Κύριε, εἰ σὺ ἐβάστασας αὐτόν, εἰπέ μοι ποῦ ἔθηκας αὐτόν, κἀγὼ αὐτὸν ἀρῶ.
20:15.targetText: Jesus says to her, “Woman, why do you weep? Whom do you seek?” She, supposing that He is the gardener, says to Him, “Lord, if You carried Him away, tell me where You laid Him, and I will take Him away”;

20:16.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς Μαριάμ. στραφεῖσα ἐκείνη λέγει αὐτῷ Ἑβραϊστί· Ῥαββουνεί (ὃ λέγεται Διδάσκαλε).
20:16.targetText: Jesus says to her, “Mary!” Having turned, she says to Him, “Rabboni!” That is to say, “Teacher.”

groups.note: Greek is called/rendered supplies the translation gloss; LSV uses the equivalent explanatory formula is to say.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 explicitly marks the response language with Hebrew/in Hebrew; LSV does not retain this language word separately.

20:17.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς Μή μου ἅπτου, οὔπω γὰρ ἀναβέβηκα πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα· πορεύου δὲ πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφούς μου καὶ εἰπὲ αὐτοῖς Ἀναβαίνω πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα μου καὶ Πατέρα ὑμῶν καὶ Θεόν μου καὶ Θεὸν ὑμῶν.
20:17.targetText: Jesus says to her, “Do not be touching Me, for I have not yet ascended to My Father; and be going on to My brothers, and say to them, I ascend to My Father and your Father, and [to] My God and your God.”

groups.note: The one written πρός governs the coordinated destination My Father and your Father and My God and your God. English repeats the same ascent-to relation with bracketed to before My God; no additional Greek preposition is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV supplies My with the first Father; N1904 has only the article at that occurrence. The later genuine My occurrences keep their own anchors.

20:18.sourceText: ἔρχεται Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ ἀγγέλλουσα τοῖς μαθηταῖς ὅτι Ἑώρακα τὸν Κύριον, καὶ ταῦτα εἶπεν αὐτῇ.
20:18.targetText: Mary the Magdalene comes, reporting to the disciples that she has seen the LORD, and [that] He said these things to her.

groups.note: Greek ὅτι introduces the reported content; English repeats the report marker in brackets for the coordinated statement about what Jesus said. Both English markers share that actual source conjunction.
N1904 gives first-person I have seen in the womans report; LSV uses third-person has seen in indirect narration. The seeing predicate is retained with that speech-person recasting explicit.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV uses third-person she with the reported seeing, while N1904 has first-person I encoded in the direct-report verb. The same woman reports the event, with the different grammatical person explicit.

20:19.sourceText: Οὔσης οὖν ὀψίας τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ τῇ μιᾷ σαββάτων, καὶ τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων ὅπου ἦσαν οἱ μαθηταὶ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἔστη εἰς τὸ μέσον, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν.
20:19.targetText: It being, therefore, evening, on that day, the first [day] of the weeks, and the doors having been shut where the disciples were assembled through fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst, and says to them, “Peace to you”;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English day explains the weekly first-day expression; no separate day noun is printed at that point.
LSV adds assembled to where the disciples were; pinned N1904 has only were without an assembling predicate.

20:20.sourceText: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἔδειξεν καὶ τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τὴν πλευρὰν αὐτοῖς. ἐχάρησαν οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ ἰδόντες τὸν Κύριον.
20:20.targetText: and having said this, He showed them His hands and side; the disciples, therefore, rejoiced, having seen the LORD.

groups.note: The Greek καί ... καί coordination presents the hands and side together; LSV uses one shared and between the two coordinated objects.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds possessive His with hands and side; N1904 has articles but no possessive pronoun there.

20:21.sourceText: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν· καθὼς ἀπέσταλκέν με ὁ Πατήρ, κἀγὼ πέμπω ὑμᾶς.
20:21.targetText: Jesus, therefore, said to them again, “Peace to you; according as the Father has sent Me, I also send you”;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

20:22.sourceText: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἐνεφύσησεν καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Λάβετε Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον.
20:22.targetText: having said this, He breathed on [them], and says to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek opens with and; LSV begins having said without retaining that opening conjunction.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English breathed-on object is supplied; no personal object pronoun is printed with breathed in N1904.

20:23.sourceText: ἄν τινων ἀφῆτε τὰς ἁμαρτίας, ἀφέωνται αὐτοῖς· ἄν τινων κρατῆτε, κεκράτηνται.
20:23.targetText: if you may forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them; if you may retain of any, they have been retained.”

20:24.sourceText: Θωμᾶς δὲ εἷς ἐκ τῶν δώδεκα, ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος, οὐκ ἦν μετ’ αὐτῶν ὅτε ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς.
20:24.targetText: And Thomas, one of the Twelve, who is called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came;

20:25.sourceText: ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ οἱ ἄλλοι μαθηταί Ἑωράκαμεν τὸν Κύριον. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἐὰν μὴ ἴδω ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτοῦ τὸν τύπον τῶν ἥλων καὶ βάλω τὸν δάκτυλόν μου εἰς τὸν τόπον τῶν ἥλων καὶ βάλω μου τὴν χεῖρα εἰς τὴν πλευρὰν αὐτοῦ, οὐ μὴ πιστεύσω.
20:25.targetText: the other disciples, therefore, said to him, “We have seen the Lord!” And he said to them, “If I may not see the mark of the nails in His hands, and may [not] put my finger into the mark of the nails, and may [not] put my hand into His side, I will not believe.”

groups.note: The one Greek μή governs the coordinated condition of seeing and putting finger/hand; LSV repeats that same condition negation in brackets with both putting predicates. All three English negatives share the genuine source negator.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

Source-witness noun difference: N1904 has the place of the nails at the second phrase, whereas LSV repeats the mark. The actual earlier τύπον stays with the first mark; place and imprint/mark are not silently conflated.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV repeats mark at the finger-insertion phrase where N1904 has place, τόπον. The first actual mark has its own earlier source word.

20:26.sourceText: Καὶ μεθ’ ἡμέρας ὀκτὼ πάλιν ἦσαν ἔσω οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ Θωμᾶς μετ’ αὐτῶν. ἔρχεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων, καὶ ἔστη εἰς τὸ μέσον καὶ εἶπεν Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν.
20:26.targetText: And after eight days, again His disciples were within, and Thomas [was] with them; Jesus comes, the doors having been shut, and He stood in the midst and said, “Peace to you!”

groups.note: The written plural ἦσαν governs the coordinated presence of the disciples and Thomas. English repeats the same copula as singular bracketed was for Thomas; this is an English agreement recast of the shared predicate, not another Greek verb.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

20:27.sourceText: εἶτα λέγει τῷ Θωμᾷ Φέρε τὸν δάκτυλόν σου ὧδε καὶ ἴδε τὰς χεῖράς μου, καὶ φέρε τὴν χεῖρά σου καὶ βάλε εἰς τὴν πλευράν μου, καὶ μὴ γίνου ἄπιστος ἀλλὰ πιστός.
20:27.targetText: Then He says to Thomas, “Bring your finger here, and see My hands, and bring your hand, and put [it] into My side, and do not become unbelieving, but believing.”

groups.note: The written hand noun is the shared object of bring and put into the side; bracketed it repeats that same hand in English.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

20:28.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Θωμᾶς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ὁ Κύριός μου καὶ ὁ Θεός μου.
20:28.targetText: And Thomas answered and said to Him, “My Lord and my God!”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds an opening And; pinned N1904 begins Thomas answered without a conjunction.

20:29.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὅτι ἑώρακάς με, πεπίστευκας; μακάριοι οἱ μὴ ἰδόντες καὶ πιστεύσαντες.
20:29.targetText: Jesus says to him, “Because you have seen Me, Thomas, you have believed; blessed [are] those having not seen, and having believed.”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly addresses Thomas by name; the name is absent from pinned N1904 at this point.
Bracketed English copula supplies the nominal blessed declaration; no corresponding Greek copula is written.

20:30.sourceText: Πολλὰ μὲν οὖν καὶ ἄλλα σημεῖα ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐνώπιον τῶν μαθητῶν, ἃ οὐκ ἔστιν γεγραμμένα ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τούτῳ·
20:30.targetText: Many indeed, therefore, other signs Jesus also did before His disciples that are not written in this scroll;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds His with disciples; N1904 has the article without a possessive pronoun.

20:31.sourceText: ταῦτα δὲ γέγραπται ἵνα πιστεύητε ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ ἵνα πιστεύοντες ζωὴν ἔχητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ.
20:31.targetText: and these have been written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing, you may have life in His Name.
